text: PSExec: Microsoft tool enabling remote command execution via hidden admin share (C$). Attackers use access rights to upload executables, execute them via Windows APIs, and retrieve results. Requires valid credentials but commonly used in red team operations.

metadata.prerequisites: Valid admin or equivalent credentials, SMB/445 connectivity, execution rights.
metadata.detection: Temporary service creation, command execution via SMB, identifiable PSExec patterns.
metadata.mitigation: Monitor C$ access, implement SMB signing, control service execution.

text: WMI Exec: Remote command execution via Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI). Attackers connect to WMI service on remote machines and execute commands using Win32_Process or Win32_Service classes. Stealthy technique leaving minimal traditional traces.

metadata.prerequisites: Valid credentials, WMI connectivity (port 135, 445), WMI access rights.
metadata.detection: Abnormal WMI activity, process creation via WMI, WMI access events.
metadata.mitigation: Restrict WMI access, monitor WMI activity, implement access controls.

text: DCOM Exec: Remote command execution via Distributed Component Object Model (DCOM). Attackers use DCOM objects like Excel.Application, Word.Application, or ShellBrowserWindow to execute code. Often used as it leverages legitimate Windows components.

metadata.prerequisites: Valid credentials, RPC/DCOM access, instantiable DCOM objects on target machine.
metadata.detection: Unusual DCOM object instantiation, abnormal RPC calls, code execution via COM.
metadata.mitigation: Disable DCOM if unnecessary, monitor RPC calls, implement COM restrictions.

text: WinRM Abuse: Exploitation of Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service for remote command execution. Attackers connect via WinRM with valid credentials and execute PowerShell or other commands. Uses ports 5985/5986.

metadata.prerequisites: Valid credentials, WinRM enabled on target, connectivity to port 5985/5986.
metadata.detection: Abnormal WinRM activity, remote PowerShell sessions, WinRM events.
metadata.mitigation: Disable WinRM if unnecessary, implement access restrictions, monitor sessions.

text: RDP Hijacking: Hijacking existing RDP sessions by attaching to active sessions. Attackers with admin access can connect to existing RDP sessions of other users without their credentials. Enables elevated access using active session rights.

metadata.prerequisites: Administrator access on target machine, RDP enabled, existing RDP session.
metadata.detection: Abnormal RDP session attachment, unusual session events, active session monitoring.
metadata.mitigation: Implement disconnected sessions, monitor RDP connections, control admin access.

text: SMB Relay: Attack relaying captured SMB authentications to other services or machines. Attackers intercept SMB authentication and relay it to another resource for access. Often combined with LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning.

metadata.prerequisites: Captured SMB authentication, network access, services accepting SMB.
metadata.detection: Abnormal SMB session relays, SMB traffic to unexpected machines, relay monitoring.
metadata.mitigation: Implement SMB signing, monitor SMB relays, implement LDAP signing.

text: Internal Spearphishing: Sending spearphishing messages targeting internal domain users to obtain credentials or install backdoors. Attackers use domain information to create convincing messages impersonating admins or IT services. Messages contain malicious links or attachments.

metadata.prerequisites: Access to internal email system or service, domain user list.
metadata.detection: Malicious emails detected by filters, suspicious URLs, malicious attachments, click monitoring.
metadata.mitigation: User awareness training, anti-phishing filters, click monitoring, domain validation.

text: BloodHound Enumeration: Complete Active Directory structure enumeration to identify attack paths. BloodHound collects user, group, ACL, and delegation information to map dependencies and privilege escalation paths.

metadata.prerequisites: Domain access, valid authentication recommended but not required.
metadata.detection: Abnormal LDAP enumeration, sensitive information access, enumeration patterns.
metadata.mitigation: Restrict anonymous LDAP queries, monitor enumeration.

text: LDAP Enumeration: Enumeration of Active Directory content via LDAP protocol to discover users, groups, computers, and resources. Attackers use LDAP queries to map domain structure and identify interesting accounts.

metadata.prerequisites: Network access to LDAP server, no authentication required for anonymous queries.
metadata.detection: Abnormal LDAP queries, extensive object enumeration.
metadata.mitigation: Restrict anonymous LDAP queries, monitor queries.

text: SPN Scanning: Enumeration of SPN (Service Principal Names) to identify available services and target service accounts. Attackers use tools to enumerate all domain SPNs and identify vulnerable services.

metadata.prerequisites: Network access to domain, LDAP queries.
metadata.detection: Extensive SPN enumeration, abnormal LDAP queries.
metadata.mitigation: Monitor SPN queries, implement LDAP restrictions.

text: GPO Enumeration: Enumeration of Group Policy Objects to identify configurations, scripts, and domain-wide settings. Attackers enumerate GPOs to find exploitation opportunities or sensitive information.

metadata.prerequisites: Access to SYSVOL share or LDAP queries.
metadata.detection: Extensive GPO enumeration, unusual SYSVOL access.

text: Trust Enumeration: Enumeration of domain trust relationships to identify neighboring domains and inter-forest lateral movement opportunities. Attackers enumerate trusts to discover accessible domains and attack paths.

metadata.detection: Extensive trust enumeration, trust LDAP queries.
metadata.mitigation: Monitor trust relationships, implement access controls.

text: DNS Zone Transfer: DNS zone transfer to obtain complete list of all domain DNS records. Attackers request zone transfer from DNS servers to enumerate network machines and services.

metadata.prerequisites: Access to DNS server, misconfigured server allowing transfers.
metadata.detection: DNS zone transfer requests, extensive DNS enumeration.
metadata.mitigation: Restrict DNS zone transfers, implement access controls.

text: Evil-WinRM: Simplified WinRM client for interactive remote PowerShell command execution on Windows servers. Evil-WinRM is useful for lateral movement and command execution.
PsExec (Sysinternals): Microsoft tool for remote process execution on Windows systems via SMB. PsExec is a classic vector for lateral movement in Active Directory.
ntlmrelayx: Impacket tool for sophisticated NTLM relay attacks. ntlmrelayx intercepts NTLM authentications and relays them to access resources.
psexec.py: Python implementation of PsExec for remote command execution via SMB. psexec.py runs on Linux and enables remote access without RDP.
wmiexec.py: Impacket script using WMI for remote command execution on Windows. wmiexec.py leaves minimal traces and is effective for lateral movement.
LDAP relay + NTLM relay: Combined techniques for relaying NTLM/LDAP authentications to AD servers. These attacks enable privilege escalation without valid credentials.
